holidays.name: National Cranberry Relish Day
holidays.description: A day to give the tart, ruby-red side dish its moment before Thanksgiving. Whether yours is a fresh-ground mix with orange zest or a sugary, spoonable blend, today is for piling it on turkey, sandwiches and anything else that needs some zing.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It lands just before Thanksgiving, when cranberry relish is at its peak.
holidays.funFact: Ripe cranberries bounce. Growers have long used this to sort good berries from bad, and it's the reason they're sometimes called bounceberries.

holidays.name: Go For a Ride Day
holidays.description: This day is a reason to get out of the house and go for a ride. Take a bike, a scooter, a horse or the passenger seat of a car, and head somewhere with no real destination. The only goal is to enjoy the trip.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages people to put down their screens and enjoy a drive or ride for its own sake.
holidays.funFact: One of the earliest bicycle ancestors was the German draisine, which Karl Drais showed off in 1817. It had no pedals, and riders pushed it along with their feet.

holidays.name: Flossing Day
holidays.description: A day to give your teeth some string-based love. Flossing Day reminds everyone to clean the gaps that a toothbrush can't reach. Pick up a pack of floss and your dentist will be happy.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is a good reminder to keep up your dental habits during the busy holiday season.
holidays.funFact: New Orleans dentist Levi Spear Parmly is widely credited with promoting the use of silk thread to clean between teeth in the early 1800s.
